Class Chip

java.lang.Object
org.adsl.client.view.gui.Chip
public final class Chip extends Object
Token-style chips for food and PP. The background image sits beneath a Christmas-Chalk number. Food is masked into a perfect circle; PP earn/loss are already octagonal PNGs with transparency and don't need masking.
  • Food: white digits with thick black external outline, anchored slightly below center over the fish/orange artwork.
  • PP positive: dark-brown digits, centered in the laurel.
  • PP negative: cream digits (including minus sign), centered.
Long values are font-scaled so 3+ char strings ("-100", "150") stay inside the laurel/circle.

Why chips are rasterised to a cached image

The chalk-font Text with an OUTSIDE stroke is expensive to rasterise (Marlin builds a stroked glyph-outline path every time the node is first drawn). The board is fully rebuilt on every interaction, so re-creating live Text nodes froze the GPU for ~1s per render on weaker iGPUs. Instead each distinct chip (type + value + width) is rendered once via Node.snapshot(SnapshotParameters, WritableImage) into an Image and cached; subsequent calls return a cheap ImageView of that image — pixel-identical, near-zero cost.
